title: Sparse Monochrome Square Components
prompt:
Implement `count_square_components(cells) -> int`. `cells` is a collection of unique `(x, y, color)` triples on an unbounded integer grid. Two cells are adjacent only when they share an edge, and a component may contain cells of only one color.

Return the number of same-color 4-connected components that are fully filled axis-aligned squares. A one-cell component counts as a square. For one component, let its bounding box have width `max_x - min_x + 1` and height `max_y - min_y + 1`; it is a square exactly when width equals height and the component contains `width * height` cells. This count rule rejects rectangles, L-shapes, and shapes with holes.

Use a hash map keyed by coordinates and BFS or DFS over present neighbors. Do not allocate a dense matrix based on coordinate magnitudes. Aim for expected O(n) time and space.

example.reasoning: The sparse coordinates form one filled 2 by 2 component.
